---
title: "Asymptotic Distribution of MLE"
---

## Background

This chapter will dive into the Asymptotic Distribution of the MLE we calculated in Chapter 1. One of the most famous statistical concepts is the central limit theorem, which establishes that as $n$ approaches infinity, every distribution approaches the Normal distribution. The original CLT can be manipulated to show that the MLE follows a Normal distribution for large $n$. It is kind of wild to think about no matter the original distribution, the distribution of the MLE approaches the Normal distribution!

## Simulating Distribution

Let's say $X_1, ...,X_n \sim \text{NegBin}(r, p)$, where $r=0.5$ and $p = \frac{1}{3}$.

We derived in Chapter 1. that $\hat{p}_{MLE} = \frac{r}{r + \bar{x}}$. Below is a histogram of $\hat{p}_{MLE}$ as $n$ grows large, in this case to $10,000$.

```{webr-r}
n_obs <- 10000  
true_size <- 0.5 #r
true_p <- 1 / 3

sims <- replicate(1000, {
  x <- rnbinom(n = n_obs, size = true_size, prob = true_p)
  x_sum <- sum(x)
  x_avg = mean(x)
  p.mle <- true_size / (true_size + x_avg)
  
  p.mle
})

sims <- t(sims)

hist_mle <- hist(sims, 
     breaks = 100, 
     main = expression("Histogram of "* hat(p)[MLE]), 
     xlab = expression(hat(p)[MLE])
)
```

## Asymptotic Calculation

Using the CLT and Taylor approximation, we showed in class that $\sqrt{n} (\hat{p}_{MLE} - p) \rightarrow N\left(0, \frac{1}{\text{Var}(\ell^\prime_{x_1}(\theta))}\right)$

Isolating for $\hat{p}_{MLE}$, we have that $\hat{p}_{MLE} \rightarrow N\left(p, \frac{1}{\text{Var}(n\ell^\prime_{x_1}(\theta))}\right)$

So, let's solve for $\text{Var}(\ell^\prime_{x_1}(\theta))}$.

Taking the score from Chapter 1, we have:

$$
\frac{d}{dp} \ell_{x_1,...,x_n}(p) = \left(\frac{rn}{p} - \frac{\sum x}{1 - p} \right)
$$

As we only want to work with one observation now, we will set $n=1$.

$$
\ell ^\prime_{x_1} (p) = \left(\frac{r}{p} - \frac{x}{1 - p} \right)
$$

We established in Chapter 2 that $\text{Var}(\ell'(\theta)) = -\mathbb{E}[\ell''(\theta)]$. This means that that the asymptotic variance of $\hat{p}_{MLE}$ is $\frac{1}{-\mathbb{E}[\ell''(\theta)]}$. So, let's solve for $-\mathbb{E}[\ell''(\theta)]$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell ^\prime_{x_1} (p) &= \frac{r}{p} - \frac{x}{1 - p}  \\
\frac{d^2}{dp^2} \ell_{x_1} (p) &= \frac{-r}{p^2} - \frac{x}{(1 - p)^2} \\
-\mathbb{E}[\ell ^{\prime \prime}_{x_1} (p)] &= \frac{r}{p^2} + \frac{\mathbb{E}[x]}{(1 - p)^2} \\
-\mathbb{E}[\ell ^{\prime \prime}_{x_1} (p)] &= \frac{r}{p^2} + \frac{\Big(\frac{r(1-p)}{p}\Big)}{(1 - p)^2} \\
-\mathbb{E}[\ell ^{\prime \prime}_{x_1} (p)] &= \frac{r}{p^2} + \frac{r}{p(1 - p)} \\
-\mathbb{E}[\ell ^{\prime \prime}_{x_1} (p)] &= \frac{r(1-p)}{p^2(1-p)} + \frac{rp}{p^2(1 - p)} \\
-\mathbb{E}[\ell ^{\prime \prime}_{x_1} (p)] &= \frac{r(1-p) + rp}{p^2(1-p)}  \\
-\mathbb{E}[\ell ^{\prime \prime}_{x_1} (p)] &= \frac{r(1 - p + p)}{p^2(1-p)}  \\
-\mathbb{E}[\ell ^{\prime \prime}_{x_1} (p)] &= \frac{r}{p^2(1-p)}  \\
\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
  \sqrt{n} (\hat{p}_{MLE} - p) \rightarrow N\left(0, \frac{p^2(1-p)}{r}\right)
$$

And again isolating for $\hat{p}_{MLE}$, we have:

$$
\hat{p}_{MLE} \overset{\cdot}{\sim} N\left(p, \frac{p^2(1-p)}{nr} \right)
$$

## Graphing Asymptotic MLE Curve

Below is a curve with the distribution of $\hat{p}_{MLE}$ with $r=0.5$, $p= \frac{1}{3}$, and large $n (10,000)$, behind a red curve displaying the asymptotically normal distribution of $\hat{p}_{MLE}$.

```{webr-r}
hist_mle <- hist(sims, 
     breaks = 100, 
     main = expression("Histogram of "* hat(p)[MLE]), 
     xlab = expression(hat(p)[MLE]),
     freq=F
)
curve(dnorm(x, mean=true_p,
            sd= sqrt( ( (true_p ** 2) * (1 - true_p) ) / (n_obs * true_size))),
add=T, col="red", lwd=2)

legend("topright", legend = expression("Asymptotic Normal "* hat(p)[MLE]), 
       col="red", lwd=2, lty = 1, cex = 0.6)
```
